paragraphs: South London is not one council area. Children in care here are looked after by the boroughs south of the Thames, among them Croydon, Lambeth, Southwark, Lewisham, Greenwich, Wandsworth, Merton, Sutton, Bromley and Kingston upon Thames, each with its own fostering service, and by the independent agencies shown above that work across several boroughs. Each borough has its own page on this site, linked below, listing the services that cover it.

Several south London boroughs have put money into supporting the carers they already have. Croydon has started Horizons Hubs, community networks of foster families each led by an experienced carer, offering peer support, planned sleepovers to give carers a break, and help in a crisis; the name was chosen by the borough's Children in Care Council. Royal Greenwich runs the Mockingbird programme, with four constellations in which a hub home with experienced carers supports a group of nearby foster families through short breaks, shared training and social activities. Lewisham has refurbished its Fostering Hub on Bromley Road in Catford as an informal base for carers and for a new team of recruiters working in the local community.

Pay varies by borough. Our Croydon page shows a 2026-27 weekly allowance of £208 to £309 for each child depending on age, plus a separate weekly skills fee for the carer starting at £325. Every fostering service in London must pay at least the national minimum allowance, which for 2026-27 is £205 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £208 for 3 to 4, £233 for 5 to 10, £266 for 11 to 15 and £309 for 16 to 17.
If you live in south London and have a spare room, speak to your own borough and to two or three of the agencies above, and ask each about training, support between visits and what they pay.
